lessons: In ms, the year constant is d * 365.25, so ms('1y') is 31557600000 — a mistake that flips * to / shrinks the parsed value below one day, which a single strictEqual on ms('1y') separates cleanly.

A broken constant in ms's parse section still parses without throwing and still formats, so the failure surfaces only as a wrong numeric return, not an error — tests must assert exact values, not just no-throw.

Changing a shared constant like y in ms propagates to every downstream expression built from it (round-trips like ms(ms('1y'))), so one direct parse assertion can be enough to prove a constant-level defect.
